meta_level_n_equals_3_series_statement.interpretation: Even in the best possible case -- all 3 series agreeing in direction -- a 3-unit sign test cannot reach one-sided alpha=0.05 (min p=1/8=0.125). The honest conclusion is unconditional: tau>=0.5 is NOT resolvable, in principle, from 3 series of this size, regardless of what the data show. This mirrors and extends the pre-registered n=10 ST-19168 finding (~41% achieved power for a SINGLE series at n=10) to the present n=3,4,5 per-series, n=3-series-of-evidence reality: small-n underpowering is a structural, recurring, honestly-disclosed property of this module's literature corroboration, not something this fire's data happened to produce.
meta_level_n_equals_3_series_statement.question: Is tau>=0.5 resolvable using the 3 series as 3 independent units of evidence?
meta_level_n_equals_3_series_statement.weakest_possible_aggregation: exact binomial sign test on 3 series-level directional point estimates

honest_power_statement.per_series_headline: At the locked target tau=0.50, one-sided alpha=0.05: asperti2024 (n=4) has ~13% asymptotic achieved power and would require an observed tau of ~0.99 to reach 80% power; zhu2022 (n=5) has ~19% achieved power and would require tau~0.95; alam2022 E-series (n=3) is combinatorially INCAPABLE of reaching alpha=0.05 one-sided significance at ANY observed tau (including a perfect tau=1.0), because with n=3 there are only 3!=6 possible permutations and the best achievable exact one-sided p-value is 1/6~0.167 > 0.05 -- this is an exact combinatorial fact, not an asymptotic approximation.
honest_power_statement.reference: Bonett & Wright 2000, Psychometrika 65(1):23-28, DOI:10.1007/BF02294183 (same formula cited in PREREGISTRATION.md and reused unchanged)
